According to a statement issued by the Clark County, Nevada, court, these include lewdness with a minor, sexual assault, and the use of a child in the production of pornography. The woman stated that she intends to testify against Stiles should the case proceed to trial. She told Phil McGraw that her daughter retains no memory of the videotaped assault, and that she had recently spoken with the girl about inappropriate touching. Although she is in a relationship with a man her daughter affectionately calls "Dad," she confessed, "I don't feel comfortable leaving her with him, nor with anybody else. ... I just cry and blame it on myself." Now eight-and-a-half months pregnant, she said the ordeal has placed considerable strain upon her. When asked whether she would rather have remained unaware of the assault, she replied, "Yes, I could have lived without knowing it."

A former girlfriend of Stiles said that, prior to his arrest, she had lived in fear after coming forward to police to identify the suspect, having recognized him from enhanced photographs of the videotape broadcast on the local news. "I've had my share of nightmares," Elaine Thomas told CNN's Nancy Grace. Thomas recalled that she screamed upon recognizing the images on television and felt she had no choice but to contact the authorities about the man she had believed to be merely a "weapons enthusiast" with only a minor criminal record.

"How could I not tell them who that man was? That little girl suffered unimaginable things, and I knew for a fact it was him," Thomas said.

"He said he'd been in the Navy and, you know, I was looking for a strong guy to represent to my sons what I thought they needed to be," Allen said.

Allen explained that she had brought Stiles to a crowded apartment where her son and daughter lived. Also residing there were a family friend and her daughter, the alleged victim of the assault. Todd Allen, Tina Allen's son, said he recognized his former apartment in scenes from the video.

One woman who had previously dated Stiles described living in terror before his capture, having approached authorities to identify the suspect after viewing enhanced images taken from the recording on a local news broadcast. "I've had my share of nightmares," Elaine Thomas said to CNN's Nancy Grace.

Thomas recounted crying out when she identified the pictures on TV, feeling she had no alternative but to reach out to police regarding a man she had believed was merely a "weapons enthusiast" with nothing more than a small criminal history.

"How could I not tell them who that man was? That little girl suffered unimaginable things, and I knew for a fact it was him," Thomas said.

"He said he'd been in the Navy and, you know, I was looking for a strong guy to represent to my sons what I thought they needed to be," Allen explained.
